question.problem: Find the surface area of the part of the surface $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x+z$ whose projection onto the $xz$-plane is bounded by $z=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)$ and the $x$-axis for $0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $y=f(x,z)$ with $(x,z)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂y}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂y}{∂z})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x+z,\,(x,z)\in D,
$$

where 

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le z\le \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221663/assets/be5dc3bf3ed4b6b7bee06d583b69e40a3922edede1e61a6f0b68d2ce0767f92a.png)

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂y}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+z)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x, \\ \frac{∂y}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+z)=1,\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂y}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂y}{∂z})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{2}+(1)^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{2+{cos}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}\sqrt{2+{cos}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{2+{cos}^{2}⁡x}\cdot z\,{|}_{z=0}^{z=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\sqrt{2+{cos}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting $u=2+{cos}^{2}⁡x,$ we get $\text{d}u=-2\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x.$ Also, the limits must be changed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & 0 & \frac{\pi }{2} \\ u & 3 & 2\end{aligned}
$$

 

Substituting these into our integral, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\sqrt{2+{cos}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =-{\int }_{3}^{2}{u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}{u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{u}^{3/2}\,{|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}({3}^{3/2}-{2}^{3/2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(3\sqrt{3}-2\sqrt{2}).\end{aligned}
$$
